title: Tiger Rag and its earlier names
summary: Lopez recalls Tiger Rag from about 1910 as Number Two or the CF and B-flat rag, and how it was played.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: I remember. Um...I was wondering about some more of that early music like the Tiger Rag. When was the first time you ever heard that or played that?
And what did they call it? Do you remember?

They called it Number 2. That was the one. Number 2 they called it. Number 2. And, uh, then the CF and B Rag. That was it. Tiger Rag. Oh, that...the Tiger Rag. Yeah. CF and B Flat. It started in the C, went to F, and then went to B Flat. Oh, Tiger Rag.
Tiger Rag. That was it. C.F and B Rag. Yeah. That's right.
That's all names we knew about. These guys come up there and somebody called it the Tiger Rag. Some guy...some lurk right around Chicago.
Yeah. Put some words to it.
Yeah. That's it. Hold that tongue again. Hold that tongue again. And they did alright too.
Yeah. And you played that with Papa Lane's groups?
Oh, yeah. That's all those guys ever knew. Mm-hmm. That's that kind of stuff there. Been played for 40 years before my time.

And, uh, it was just more hoedown stuff, you know, than anything else. Yeah. And, of course, as the fellas went along, they interpreted a little new tricks into it, and this, that, and the other. I hear some of the bands playing Tiger Rag today. Ooh, you wouldn't recognize it.
You know, they've got a different tune altogether.
